title: THE SECURE PENDING BOX
goal: Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.
steps: 1. Imagine Container — Imagine a container whose lock, size, material, and location feel credible. Secure Pending — breathe naturally.
2. Place Cannot — Place only what cannot be processed now inside it.
3. Name Stored — Name what is stored and when it will be revisited, ideally with support. Secure Pending — name sensation.
4. Close Container — Close the container and reorient to the next task for today. Secure Pending — next action.

title: BUILD SAFE-ENOUGH, NOT PERFECT
goal: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
steps: 1. Place Five — Construct a place using five sensory facts and one control feature: an exit, boundary, companion, or adjustable distance. Build Safe — move slowly.
2. Rehearse Specific — Rehearse entering through a specific cue and leaving on purpose. Build Safe — name sensation.
3. Strengthen — Strengthen the detail that produces the clearest bodily yes. Build Safe — next action.

title: ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH
goal: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
steps: 1. Apply Quiet — As events arise, apply a quiet category: hearing, planning, heat, remembering, pressure. Word Light — hear sound.
2. Use Word — Use one word once, then return to the raw event. Word Light — allow opposite.
3. Name Producing — If a Name starts producing analysis, Name that ‘explaining’ and release it. Word Light — next action.

title: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
goal: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
steps: 1. Choose Precise — Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks. Close Micro — widen gaze.
2. Return Instead — Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
3. Track Interval — Track the interval between noticing and reconnection. Close Micro — notice detail.
4. Let Practice — Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps. Close Micro — next action.

title: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
goal: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
steps: 1. Pick Word — Choose one harmless five-letter word, such as TABLE. Use each letter once; there is no need to finish perfectly. Break Night — feel support.
2. Call Object — For the first letter, name a neutral object beginning with it—T for tree, for example.
3. Flash Image — Picture that object for about two seconds with no action, meaning, memory, or story. Break Night — allow opposite.
4. Jump Letter — Jump to the next letter and a completely unrelated object. End after five letters; do not score sleep. Break Night — next action.

title: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
goal: A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.
steps: 1. Throwaway — Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING. Make First — feel support.
2. Make Wrong — Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, messy mental sketch, or unfinished opening.
3. Fix One — Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest. Make First — allow opposite.
4. Continue Clean — Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly. Make First — next action.

title: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
goal: Judge the mental move by how it treats your life.
steps: 1. Ask Thought — Ask the current thought three questions: Does it clarify the next move?. Ally Saboteur — press feet.
2. Check Protection — Does it protect something real?
3. Leave Me — Does it leave me more capable afterward?. Ally Saboteur — pick action.
4. Score Yes — Score each yes or no.
5. Thank Warning — If it fails two, thank the warning and appoint a different inner adviser. Ally Saboteur — next action.

title: STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION
goal: Some mental worlds persist through continuous subscription.
steps: 1. Identify Image — Spot the image, conclusion, or demand being refreshed. Stop Renewing — feel support.
2. Time — For one minute, refuse only the renewal: no new scene, argument, or confirmation.
3. Let Existing — Let existing residue fade at its own rate. Stop Renewing — name sensation.
4. Redirect — Redirect the freed attention into a chosen sensory task. Stop Renewing — next action.

title: PRECISE OUTSIDE, QUIET INSIDE
goal: Action can be sharp without inner warfare.
steps: 1. Define — Set the exact external behaviour required. Precise Outside — soften shoulders.
2. Execute — Execute it with full timing and skill.
3. Imagine Applause — Meanwhile, decline the running argument about authorship, resentment, or imagined applause. Precise Outside — notice detail.
4. Let Body — Allow the body act and the inner courtroom remain closed until the task ends. Precise Outside — next action.

title: SELF-RESPECT CHECKSUM

steps: 1. Respond Verify — Before responding, verify four conditions: fair to both sides; no apology for merely existing or setting a limit; aligned with your values; completely truthful. Self Respect — loosen hands.
2. Revise Sentence — Revise any sentence that fails the checksum. Self Respect — split duty.
3. Speak Extra — Then speak without extra justification. Self Respect — next action.

title: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
goal: Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.
steps: 1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you. Say Mind — loosen hands.
2. Say What Happened — In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Do Not Edit — Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm. Say Mind — notice detail.
4. Wait — Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind. Say Mind — next action.

title: THE TWENTY-MINUTE TRUTH STORY
goal: A private story can help your mind make sense of an event.
steps: 1. Set A Time — Choose up to twenty minutes. Twenty Minute — widen gaze.
2. Tell The Story — In your mind, move through what occurred, what you felt, and what it means now.
3. Come Back To Now — End by naming your location, today’s date, and one caring action you can take. Twenty Minute — allow opposite.
4. Repeat Only If Helpful — Try again on another day only if it helps. Twenty Minute — next action.

title: CROSS OUT THE EXPIRED FUTURE
goal: A forecast should lose influence when its decision window closes.
steps: 1. Picture Prediction — Picture the prediction and the exact condition that makes it obsolete: date passed, result known, action completed, evidence changed. Cross Out — soften shoulders.
2. Imagine Line — When that condition arrives, Imagine a line through the forecast and Picture EXPIRED. Cross Out — add counterfact.
3. Remove Vote — It may remain historically visible, but it receives no further vote. Cross Out — next action.

title: THE LIFE RETURNED TEST
goal: Imagine receiving this ordinary day back.
steps: 1. Picture — Picture having lost access to your current life and unexpectedly waking inside it again. Life Returned — widen gaze.
2. Small — What small feature would suddenly matter—someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, morning light?. Life Returned — notice detail.
3. Choose Behaviour — Choose one behaviour that honours that recovered value today, without romanticising real hardship. Life Returned — next action.

1. Picture Tomorrow — Picture as tomorrow-you, after tonight’s urge has passed: ‘Please protect at least…’ Name one minimum—sleep, money, sobriety, dignity, preparation, or safety. Note From — hear sound.

3. Place Contract — Place Contract the contract where the immediate choice occurs. Note From — next action.

✓ I can let the consequence-bearer make one request.

Picture Tomorrow → Date Sign → Place Contract

PAUSE
Use live support when an urge threatens serious harm or relapse.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LOOK FOR THE MISSING DANGER
goal: Absence becomes evidence only after prediction says what should be present.
steps: 1. Ask Sign — Ask what sign must exist right now if the feared model is correct. Look Missing — soften shoulders.
2. Search Fairly — Search once, fairly.
3. Mark Absence — If it is absent, Keep that absence and reduce—not erase—the model’s weight. Look Missing — notice detail.
4. Name Explanation — Name the alternate explanation strengthened by the missing sign. Look Missing — next action.

title: THREE ACTIVE FUTURES ONLY
goal: Forecasts must compete for limited shelf space.
steps: 1. Picture Predictions — Picture the three predictions currently most relevant. Three Active — hear sound.
2. Enter Retiring — Any new forecast may enter only by retiring one, merging with one, or proving higher usefulness for a decision.
3. Cross Out — Remove retired entries from view. Three Active — notice detail.
4. Act Portfolio — Act from the remaining portfolio rather than unlimited mental possibilities. Three Active — next action.

title: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
goal: Charge felt importance rent before it enters the decision.
steps: 1. Score Information — Score the information on two separate axes: how noticeable it feels and how much it changes the choice. Vivid Important — soften shoulders.
2. Pay Felt — A dramatic item with low relevance pays a felt importance tax and moves down the Name. Vivid Important — notice detail.
3. Allocate Attention — Allocate attention to decision impact instead. Vivid Important — next action.

title: MEASURE THE EMOTION’S VELOCITY
goal: Intensity is a photograph; momentum is the film.
steps: 1. Set Level — At three intervals, Keep not only level but direction and speed: rising fast, steady, falling slowly. Measure Emotion — soften shoulders.
2. Add Action — Add the action impulse at each point. Measure Emotion — name feeling.
3. Make Decisions — Make decisions from trajectory plus facts, not from the first intensity number alone. Measure Emotion — next action.

2. Imagine Arrows — Imagine arrows from the present feeling back to its actual sources. Return Each — name sensation.
3. Stop Blaming — Address the largest actionable contributor first; stop blaming the most visible issue for unrelated load. Return Each — next action.

2. Choose Opposite — Choose an opposite rhythm: agitated becomes deliberate, collapsed becomes lightly brisk, looping becomes irregular. Change Rhythm — notice detail.
3. Observe Emotional — Maintain the new tempo through one simple task and observe the emotional shift. Change Rhythm — next action.

Goal: Emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story.
Game Move: PLAY: Cadence → Choose Opposite → Observe Emotional
Goal + Steps:
GOAL
Emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story.

1. Cadence — Notice the cadence of speech, movement, or breathing. Change Rhythm — soften shoulders.
2. Choose Opposite — Choose an opposite rhythm: agitated becomes deliberate, collapsed becomes lightly brisk, looping becomes irregular. Change Rhythm — notice detail.
3. Observe Emotional — Maintain the new tempo through one simple task and observe the emotional shift. Change Rhythm — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Observe Emotional.
Win / Reward: ✓ Emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story.
Formula Flow: Cadence → Choose Opposite → Observe Emotional
Safety:
PAUSE
Match movement to medical ability and avoid breath manipulation if activating.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE
goal: Pain may be stored without its later survival chapter.
steps: 1. End Retell — Retell only enough to reach the painful ending. Memory Does — move slowly.
2. Follow Escape — Then append what actually followed: escape, help, adaptation, learning, regained ability, or today’s status.
3. Don't Invent — Do not invent redemption. Memory Does — notice detail.
4. Restore — Restore the omitted chronology. Memory Does — next action.

title: SAY THE SENTENCE HISTORY NEVER RECEIVED
goal: Symbolic completion can end a language loop without rewriting facts.
steps: 1. Picture Words — Picture the exact words you could not say or hear. Say Sentence — hear sound.
2. Speak Empty — Say them quietly in your mind or to an empty room while clearly stating that this is present-day completion, not a changed past. Say Sentence — pick action.
3. Add Response — Add the response current-you can now provide. Say Sentence — next action.

2. Let It Lead — Start with that small step and let it naturally lead into the main task. Let It Lead next. Through Side — pick action. Through Side — next action.

title: PUT THE FIRST OBJECT IN THE PATH
goal: Let the space issue a clear instruction.
steps: 1. Identify Object — Spot the first object the desired behaviour requires. Put First — move slowly.
2. Position — Position it where normal movement will encounter it at the right time.
3. Remove Competing — Remove competing cues from that path. Put First — pick action.
4. Meet — When you meet the object, perform the linked first action before walking past. Put First — next action.

title: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
goal: Imbalance becomes negotiable after it becomes visible.
steps: 1. Plan Carries — Across a defined period, tally who initiates, accommodates, repairs, plans, and carries emotional follow-up. Map Relationship — soften shoulders.
2. Add Context — Include background for genuine capacity differences. Map Relationship — split forecast.
3. Use Categories — Discuss the pattern using categories, not accusations, and request one clear rebalance. Map Relationship — next action.

title: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
goal: A safer choice may be the mistake you can see early enough to correct.
steps: 1. Name Options — Name the two or three live options. For each, Picture the specific way it could fail—not a vague fear. Choose Easiest — breathe naturally.
2. Name Failure — Name the earliest observable sign that failure has begun. It must be visible or clear, not a feeling alone.
3. Warning — State what corrective action would still be available when that sign appears and what cost has already accumulated. Choose Easiest — name feeling.
4. Choose Visible — Choose the option whose reliable warning arrives while correction is still practical. Use this as one decision criterion, not the whole verdict. Choose Easiest — next action.

title: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
goal: Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.
steps: 1. Rest Gaze — Rest your gaze on a stable line, corner, or heavy object. Borrow Stillness — breathe naturally.
2. Compare Visual — Compare its visual constancy with the motion inside your body and mind.
3. Don't Match — Do not make the inner movement match. Borrow Stillness — name sensation.
4. Let Facts — Let both facts coexist until the outer reference becomes usable. Borrow Stillness — next action.

title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
goal: Urgency shrinks when hearing regains depth.
steps: 1. Identify Nearest — Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer. Sort Sounds — move slowly.
2. Move Attention — Move attention outward through those distances, then back once. Sort Sounds — pick action.
3. Let Far — Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one. Sort Sounds — next action.

title: HIDE THE OPTION NAMES
goal: See what the options look like before their names start campaigning.
steps: 1. Mask Names — Ask someone—or a shuffled Notice—to rename the leading options A, B and C without showing which is which. Hide Option — soften shoulders.
2. Choose Traits — Choose three relevant traits, such as cost, time, fit, reliability, or learning. Keep safety facts visible.
3. Rank Blind — Compare the symbols on those traits without guessing their identities and Hold the current order. Hide Option — split forecast.
4. Reveal Options — Reveal the names. Keep the blind order or name exactly what Name changed it and why. Hide Option — next action.

3. Finish The Block — Complete that block before changing to a different kind of task. Group By — next action.

title: WHAT KIND OF EFFORT IS THIS?
goal: Difficulty can signal growth, danger, novelty, or bad design.
steps: 1. Use Evidence — Classify the strain using evidence. Kind Effort — feel support.
2. Stop Novelty — If danger, stop; if novelty, allow learning; if skill growth, dose it; if poor design, simplify the system. Kind Effort — notice detail.
3. Respond Category — Respond to the category instead of interpreting all effort as failure. Kind Effort — next action.

title: SWAP OUTCOME CONTROL FOR PROCESS CONTROL
goal: Measure what your hands can actually influence.
steps: 1. Name Desired — Name the desired outcome and cross it out as the score. Swap Outcome — widen gaze.
2. Practise Applications — Substitute one visible process variable fully under your control—calls made, honest minutes practised, applications sent, boundary delivered. Swap Outcome — allow opposite.
3. Evaluate — Check success only on that variable for the chosen period. Swap Outcome — next action.

title: SOFTEN BOTH SIDES OF SEEING
goal: Perceiver and perceived need not stay rigidly opposed.

3. Place Reality — Refuse to place all reality on either side. Soften Both — notice detail.
4. Let Relationship — Let the relationship event—seeing or hearing—become primary for several seconds. Soften Both — next action.
